capabilities.title: Extract code structure and cross-file relationships locally with tree-sitter across many languages
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README What it does and supported language inventory
capabilities.reason: Nexus is a TypeScript and JavaScript product and its project graph is deliberately scoped to active source roots. Vendoring dozens of language parsers would add a general code-indexing platform unrelated to the current repository.

capabilities.title: Combine code, documents, SQL schemas, office files, images, audio, and video in one graph
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README overview, optional extras, and supported input sections
capabilities.reason: Automatically ingesting private documents and media, then optionally sending semantic content to a model, conflicts with Nexus's explicit local-source and retention boundaries.

capabilities.title: Label every graph relationship as extracted or inferred
Detect communities and highly connected concepts without requiring an LLM
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README God nodes and Communities capability rows
capabilities.adaptationNotes: Nexus deterministically reports connected import communities and coupling-based central files for its bounded local dependency graph.

capabilities.title: Query the saved graph, explain a concept, and trace paths between concepts
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README query, explain, and path command examples

capabilities.title: Write graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, and interactive graph.html artifacts
Install host-specific assistant skills for Codex and many other coding tools
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README Install and supported platform table
capabilities.reason: Nexus does not modify external assistant profiles. Its project graph is available through native protected routes and checked repository scripts.

capabilities.title: Install hooks or instruction files that direct assistants to query the graph before broad source searches
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README Make your assistant always use the graph
capabilities.reason: An optional graph tool must not rewrite AGENTS.md, hooks, or operator instructions. Repository instructions remain human-governed.

capabilities.title: Expose graph queries through an optional MCP server
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README optional mcp extra and pyproject.toml graphify-mcp entry point
capabilities.reason: Nexus already exposes bounded graph, explanation, and path operations through its authenticated project API. A second MCP process would duplicate the native route and add another authentication surface.

capabilities.title: Push graph data to optional Neo4j or FalkorDB backends
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README optional extras and pyproject.toml exporter dependencies
capabilities.reason: The current Nexus slice is local-first and does not need a second graph database service for the department map.

capabilities.title: Use Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, or Azure backends for semantic passes
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README backend extras and optional semantic processing
capabilities.reason: The Nexus project graph is deterministic and model-free. Any general AI call belongs behind lib/ai.ts, but adding a semantic document and media graph pass is outside this bounded code-relationship feature.
